scope: abstract finite scheduling model only; no RTL/board/software build
goal: Execute all four/eight groups, test equal-resource ordinary controls, expose whether consumer-ACK-aware closure adds decisions beyond shared-setup batching.

resources.source_key: (context,stage,access,epoch,page); all examples explicitly one legal translation domain; no cross-context free reuse
resources.destination: one explicitly paid hot target translation entry; all destinations within that legal hot page; this model cannot claim cold-target or actual combined-IOTLB results
resources.copy_completion: each fragment has unique payload and independent READ+WRITE+B/visibility completion; service duration d charged to every fragment
resources.reserve: reserve the entire fragment at copy dispatch; release only at group consumer ACK
resources.source_mapping: static successful authority; no fault/remap/coherence conclusion

executor.interface: simulate(case, ordered_descriptor_ids, overlap=False, drain=False) -> {status, last_copy_time, cache, completed_ids, ready, ack, metrics, trace}; replay prefix from reset for branch scoring is allowed because <=16 descriptors. Prefix does not flush future ACKs to change last_copy_time. Full run drain=True completes all actual ACKs.
executor.serial: At each next descriptor, complete any required source walk then allocate B and copy for d. Source cache LRU with insertion only at walk completion. Advance time while processing already scheduled ACKs. Source walk can run while buffer is full; copy dispatch cannot borrow a future ACK.
executor.overlap: Same immediate-successor one-walk lookahead for ALL policies. Once current copy dispatch latches own authority and allocates buffer, begin required source walk for the next descriptor concurrently with this copy, using the same walk engine/cache. Wait for both previous copy and next authority as necessary. No extra durable mapping token/cache slot. Current copy authority may legally outlive cache eviction, but no later copy may reuse it. Do not look beyond one successor. Emit walk-start/end/cache eviction and allocation/ACK traces.
executor.events: At time t process all copy completions and ACKs before new dispatch. On group's last copy completion schedule consumer FIFO service max(ready,last_consumer_end), duration per group. Pending ACK can release slots only at its scheduled actual time. If full buffer and no pending ACK, prefix/order is infeasible, not a silent deadlock or an ordinary baseline loss.
executor.prefix_prediction: All planners receive identical sealed descriptors and known fixed service costs; policy forecasting is a static-model idealisation, not runtime latency clairvoyance claim. Overlap evaluator may see only successor contained in the proposed prefix; final full orders give every policy identical cross-plan lookahead.

policies.group_first: Select oldest unfinished group. Pick its next source page in declared descriptor order, page-batch remaining descriptors in age order. For any addition that cannot finish its own group immediately, leave at least one free incoming slot, counting in-flight/live inputs; skip unsafe head and prefer a page that closes the oldest partial group. Complete group plans if page-batch fallback needed. Must reproduce X,Y1,Y2,Y3,Z1,Z2,Z3 on 4-group serial fixture.
policies.hot_page: Select largest number of remaining descriptors sharing a source key, ties oldest group/page declaration order. Same safe incoming reserve and partial-group completion fallback as group_first. In eight-group serial case first W1,W2,W3 then U1, no W4 when this would occupy all four slots. It must complete all groups legally.
policies.closure_ack_density: For remaining groups bucket exact remaining source-key set (<=2). Enumerate each age prefix and both page orders; order descriptors by page then group age. Probe common executor for capacity-feasible prefix extension. Score newly-ready groups divided by elapsed production duration through final copy (includes actual ACK wait); highest, then older group, lower extra walk count, lexicographic order. Continue until all descriptors issued. No fixed fairness-cycle claim for this finite sealed workload.
policies.max_closure: Cheap ordinary control: enumerate one/two source-key unions and age prefixes of all remaining groups whose remaining keys fit the union; legal common-executor capacity gate. Rank number newly-ready groups first, then fewer distinct cold setups, fewer copied fragments, oldest group. Does not score predicted ACK wait. The union may combine different exact-key buckets.
policies.setup_density: Strong ordinary setup-batch control: same one/two-key union candidates as max_closure, capacity-feasible; score number completed / (estimated missing-key setup cost + sum full-copy service). Current cached keys count hot; no ACK wait in score. Tie oldest group, fewer extra walks. This is deliberately a concrete non-ACK-aware contender, not a straw baseline.
policies.marginal_unlock_proxy: DARTS-inspired mapping only, never label faithful execution of StarPU/DARTS: choose one-key batch by transfer/setup cost divided by consumer work immediately unlocked by that batch; if none, choose oldest feasible one-group two-key closure. Keep exact same authority/cache/copy/ACK resource contract. Full genuine DARTS data-object lifetime and startup rules are not represented; evidence boundaries must be explicit.

acceptance.hand_four_serial: X-first explicit order ready [11,35,37,38], ACK [12,36,38,39]; YZ-first ready [24,26,27,38], ACK [25,27,28,39]; both makespan39; source walks3/copies7/peak<=4. The closure policy must match YZ-first in this fixture.
acceptance.hand_eight_prefix: Explicit W1,W2,W3,U1 has first H1 ready24/ACK25 in serial cap1; explicit Y1,Y2,Y3,Z1,Z2,Z3 has ACK25,27,28. Then execute every remaining descriptor and consumer, not only early prefix.
acceptance.invariants: All descriptor payload copies exactly once; own successful translation at dispatch; reserved/live total<=B at every event; ready requires all actual full copies; no release before consumer ACK; one consumer; each declared group<=B; finite all-group termination.
acceptance.negative_checks: Provide focused unittest checks that reject full-pool unfinished-head prefix, detect duplicate descriptor, verify no future ACK borrowing, serial hand timing, and same overlap opportunity for controls.
acceptance.reports: Full all-group ready/ACK arrays, mean_ACK, makespan, total full copies, source walks, peak buffer, capacity wait, completion curve, exact policy orders. Group_first/hot_page must not 'lose by deadlock': fix ordinary safe implementation or mark invalid comparison. Differences are abstract service units, not DUT cycles.
acceptance.limits: No hardware speed/area claim, no application evidence claim, no independent novelty based on a proxy. Stop after these six fixtures x two profiles x six policies; no broad sweeps or unnecessary observers.

delivery: Complete Python source as named code blocks c_event_model.py, c_policies.py, run_c_model.py, test_c_model.py; no shell tools assumed. Complete implementation and acceptance checks, assumptions and any bounded gaps. Do not invent measured outputs; root will run.
